question: what is the difference between the barrett m82 and m107
answer: The Barrett M82 and M107 are essentially the same weapon, with the M107 being the standardized version by the U.S. military. The main difference lies in their designations; the M107 is the standardized version of the M82. Both are semi-automatic anti-materiel sniper systems developed by Barrett Firearms Manufacturing. The M107 is known as the "Light Fifty" and is used by some armed forces as an anti-personnel system. The M107 uses a .50 BMG chambering and has features like a Leupold 4.5-14×50 Mark 4 scope.

retrieved_context.title: Barrett M82
retrieved_context.text: The Barrett M107 is a . 50 caliber , shoulder - fired , semi-automatic sniper rifle . Like its predecessors , the rifle is said to have manageable recoil for a weapon of its size owing to the barrel assembly that itself absorbs force , moving inward toward the receiver against large springs with every shot . Additionally , the weapon 's weight and large muzzle brake also assist in recoil reduction . Various changes were made to the original M82A1 to create the M107 , with new features such as a lengthened accessory rail , rear grip , and monopod socket . Barrett has recently been asked to develop a lightweight version of the M107 under the Anti-Materiel Sniper Rifle Congressional Program , and has already come up with a scheme to build important component parts such as the receiver frame and muzzle brake out of lighter - weight materials .
